summary: A Postgres-centric alert ingestion and incident-routing system with transactional durability, idempotent incident/job creation via unique constraints, and worker-based processing using SKIP LOCKED. It covers key alerting primitives (dedupe/grouping, silences, inhibition, escalation policies, SLO burn-rate generation) and has a credible overload strategy for alert storms with tenant guardrails and safe-mode behavior.
strengths: Clear correctness invariants with strong transactional boundaries (durable acceptance, serialized incident mutations, audited config changes).
Practical operational detail: storm protection, retry/backoff with dead-lettering and replay, and concrete latency/availability targets with monitoring/runbooks.
weaknesses: Postgres-as-queue at stated burst rates risks hot-spotting and operational limits (locking contention, vacuum/IO pressure, large partitions/indexes), likely needing sharding or an external log/queue at higher scale.

Some hard problems are underspecified for production (rule evaluation performance/complexity, on-call schedule resolution edge cases, cross-region/residency strategy, provider rate limits and global fanout controls).
